messages:
maria (Marketing): Hey team — need a tight narrative for the benchmark we want to push next week. Goal: clear latency vs cost story for engineers evaluating inference platforms. Quick sync?
jon (Product): Short checklist: 1) single-tenant vs shared baseline 2) p50/p95/p99 charts 3) cost per 1k tokens for typical seq lengths 4) clear call-to-action for trials.
kevin (Eng): Agreed. For data we should use two workloads: chat (avg seq 512) and completion (avg seq 128). We'll run on A100-80GB + quantized bf16/4-bit to show tradeoffs.
amy (Content): Can we make one simple slide that says "Same quality, 2x lower cost at p95"? Need a headline + 2 supporting bullets.
sam (Data): I can run a quick sweep today. Bench-bot: job #4721 started (config: 1xA100, batch-size range 1-32, kv-cache enabled). ETA ~35m.
maria (Marketing): Nice. For the narrative, I want three frames: 1) frictionless onboarding + throughput, 2) unit economics (cost/token) by model/config, 3) reliability/fallback story. The benchmark should feed the 2nd frame.
jon (Product): Also include a small table called "What this means" mapping numbers to product decisions (e.g., 50ms p95 -> interactive UI ok; 200ms p95 -> background inference).
kevin (Eng): One caution: we must be careful not to claim absolute numbers that depend on customer infra. Use phrasing: "in our tests" and publish configs. And include code block for config: ```yaml
model: open-llama-7b
precision: q4_0
batching: continuous
hw: a100-80gb
prompts: synthetic-dialog-512
```
amy (Content): Love the config snippet. For visuals: one line chart (p95 latency vs throughput), one bar chart (cost per 1k tokens for each quant/profile). I can mock in Figma. Link: https://figma.com/redwood/bench-draft (will update).
sam (Data): Early numbers: chat workload p95 = 82ms at 200 tps (A100 q4_0), cost = $0.27 per 1k tokens. Completion workload p95 = 34ms at 500 tps, cost = $0.11 per 1k tokens.
maria (Marketing): Those look promising. Let's add a small comparison column vs a managed competitor baseline (public numbers) but call it "typical managed endpoint" to avoid naming. Keep it high level.
jon (Product): For the blog/launch, include a short methodology appendix: dataset (synthetic+open prompts), warmup policy, KV cache hits, and how we measured cost (cloud price + GPU amortization).
kevin (Eng): Also add a note about fallbacks — show a tiny flow diagram: primary: high-perf quantized model -> fallback: higher-precision variant -> fallback: different region. That supports reliability claims.
amy (Content): I'll draft 500-word narrative + three tweet-sized blurbs for social. Can someone drop the chart PNGs by EOD?
sam (Data): Will push CSVs and PNGs to the drive: https://drive.google.com/redwood/bench/1767765432 (uploading).
maria (Marketing): Great. Responsibility matrix: sam -> data/PNGs, kevin -> config + methodology blurb, jon -> product framing + CTA, amy -> write + social. We'll review at 4pm.
bench-bot: job #4721 completed. Artifacts: results.csv, p95_plot.png, cost_bar.png.
maria (Marketing): Perfect — Amy, grab p95_plot.png and spin two headline options: one emphasizing latency, one emphasizing cost. We'll A/B in the campaign.
amy (Content): On it. Drafts by 3:30pm.
jon (Product): One last ask — include an embeddable JSON of the benchmark metadata (model, hw, batch, prompt) so readers can reproduce. Sam will that be ok?
sam (Data): Yes — I'll add metadata.json to the drive.
maria (Marketing): Cool. If everything looks good at review we'll schedule the blog + webinar blurb for next Tuesday. Thanks all :rocket:
